meta.use_when: You need the leanest possible sign-in — one email field that sends a one-time code, no password.
meta.not_for: you're collecting a password, not sending a one-time code — this pattern has no password field at all → login; you want a provider-first flow instead of email-only → login-oauth; the user already submitted their email and you're now showing the six-digit code entry — that's a separate step from this one → otp-verification

docs: The bare-minimum sign-in — no card chrome, a single email field, sign-in by one-time code. Do: Reserve the bare, uncontained layout for cases where the surrounding page or modal already frames it. Don't: Drop this pattern directly onto a busy page background with nothing to separate it visually. Use login when you're collecting a password, not sending a one-time code — this pattern has no password field at all. Use login-oauth when you want a provider-first flow instead of email-only. Use otp-verification when the user already submitted their email and you're now showing the six-digit code entry — that's a separate step from this one.
